forces.title: Rising tourist arrivals boost hospitality real estate demand
forces.description: India recorded 9.15 million foreign tourist arrivals in 2025, with projections to reach 30.5 million by 2028. Domestic tourism is also strong, supported by thematic circuits under government schemes. This surge in tourist activity directly drives demand for hotel real estate (a component of Specialty Real Estate), leading to increased occupancies and a robust development pipeline for property owners and investors in the segment.

forces.title: RBI allows bank lending to REITs, boosting real estate liquidity
forces.description: In February 2026, the Reserve Bank of India permitted banks to lend to REITs, subject to regulatory safeguards. This measure is crucial for enhancing liquidity and enabling long-term financing for income-generating real estate assets across all segments, including potentially diversified and specialty real estate portfolios. It provides a more robust funding environment, fostering growth and institutional participation in these asset classes.

forces.title: Real estate developers diversify portfolios across multiple asset classes
forces.description: Real estate developers are increasingly expanding their portfolios to include residential, office, retail, logistics & industrial, data centers, and "alternative asset classes." This strategic shift, driven by evolving market demand, represents a structural move towards diversification. For the "Diversified Real Estate Conglomerates" segment, this trend indicates a growing number of entities adopting multi-asset strategies, reducing reliance on single dominant asset types and creating more resilient portfolios.

forces.title: Budget proposes dedicated REITs for CPSE assets, unlocking value
forces.description: The Union Budget 2026-27 proposes dedicated Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) for Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE)-owned assets. This initiative aims to accelerate the monetisation of underutilised government real estate and unlock significant value. For the diversified real estate segment, this represents a substantial opportunity for new asset portfolios, potentially incorporating various asset classes and expanding the institutional investment landscape beyond traditional segments.

viewpoints.title: Strong investor confidence drives robust hospitality real estate development pipeline
viewpoints.description: IBEF highlights strong investor confidence in India’s hospitality real estate sector, evidenced by 586 branded hotel signings in 2025, adding 64,118 keys to the development pipeline. Hotel occupancies are expected to grow at a CAGR of 3.5-4%, adding 15,000-16,000 premium branded rooms. This reflects a positive outlook for property owners and developers in the hotel real estate segment, driven by expanding high-quality accommodation into Tier II and III cities.

demand_drivers.description: Rising internet penetration structurally drives demand for robust telecom infrastructure, directly impacting the AUM and growth of telecom tower InvITs.
A nearly two-fold increase in data usage provides a strong and sustained structural demand for telecom towers, supporting their large-scale operations and investment appeal.

pnl_drivers.description: Telecom tower InvITs demonstrate stable operating metrics, including a consistent tenancy ratio of approximately 1.40 times during FY25, contributing to predictable income and financial performance.

market_sizing.methodology: Asset Under Management (AUM) for telecom tower InvITs as of March 31, 2025, comprising 2.57 lakh towers and 1.7 million route km of fibre assets. This represents a significant portion of the total InvIT AUM.
market_sizing.source_title: India’s InvITs AUM to reach Rs 7.25-7.50 lakh crore by FY26

demand_drivers.description: The growing trend of nuclear families increases the need for specialized senior housing solutions, as traditional multi-generational living arrangements become less common.
Rapid urbanization contributes to the demand for dedicated senior living communities and facilities within or near urban centers.

market_sizing.methodology: Market size projection for senior citizen housing in India by 2030, based on a study by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

demand_drivers.description: FTAs in India are expected to reach 15.3 million by 2025, which will directly lead to a significant increase in demand for hotel accommodations and service apartments.

Spiritual tourism accounts for nearly 60% of domestic travel in India, representing a large, untapped market that will drive demand for hospitality real estate in key pilgrimage and cultural destinations.

new_opportunities.description: A projected spurt in hotel occupancies and the addition of approximately 15,000-16,000 premium branded rooms signal substantial opportunities for hotel real estate asset owners.
Growing demand for service apartments, driven by increased tourism, presents opportunities for asset owners, particularly within the unorganized sector to meet accommodation needs.

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of increased foreign tourist arrivals and the growth of spiritual tourism in India, driving demand for hospitality real estate assets.

demand_drivers.description: India needs to add 2 million hospital beds to reach the global average of 2.6 beds per 1,000 people, creating substantial demand for the development and ownership of healthcare real estate facilities.

market_sizing.methodology: Assessment of the existing deficit in hospital beds in India compared to global averages, indicating significant unmet demand for healthcare real estate.
